newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European mkts slip, fear to follow U.S. rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European mkts slip, fear to follow U.S. rise.

text.p: European stock markets ended mixed to lower on Thursday, fearing to follow an opening rally on Wall Street, despite widespread relief that U.S. consumer prices for July showed no inflationary threat to the roaring bull market.
Both London and German share markets closed below psychological support points, which may presage further declines.

The dollar rallied after piercing a big chart resistance point at 116.80 yen, touching 118 yen on heavy buying. This helped it to retrieve losses against the mark too, as one piece of U.S. economic data after another showed the U.S. economy could plough ahead leaving barely a ripple in inflation.

"The figures were in line, and now everyone is watching the currency market," said one share dealer in London. "Everyone is looking for a correction, but whether the catalyst will be the currency or Wall Street or whatever I don't know."

July U.S. consumer prices rose 0.2 percent as expected, as did July industrial output. Capacity use fell to 83.1 percent in July from a revised 83.3 percent in June, showing that the U.S. economy is expanding the engine to power its economy even faster than it hits the accelerator.

"With capacity utilization down to 83.1 percent, we are even further away from the inflationary pressure point than we were before this release. This will not do anything to change the Federal Reserve's view (that interest rates do not need to rise)," said Lou Crandall, chief economist at R.H. Wrightson.
Wall Street quickly jumped to a 60 point gain on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, but as London's share market closed the Dow had trimmed its gains to 26 points at 7955.

The pound remained stubbornly above 2.90 marks which restrained British shares. The strong pound makes British exports less competitive abroad and allows foreign rivals to price keenly in the U.K. market.

London shares reversed early gains, and the FTSE-100 index of leading shares fell 12.3 to 4991.3, breaking back down through the psychological 5000 level for the first time since hurdling the barrier last week.
The Paris bourse ended mixed after a 2.5 percent drop on Wednesday, as investors squared their books and packed up for the mid-August long weekend.
German shares in late electronic trade extended losses seen in the main bourse session, and the IBIS-DAX index dented an important support point at 4,200 by trading around 4195 by the close.
The dollar was quoted around 1.8423 marks and 117.67 yen, compared with 1.8547 and 117.70 in late European trading on Wednesday.
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 12.3 points at 4,991.3.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed 47.05 points weaker at 4,231.43
PARIS - The CAC-40 index finished 2.20 lower at 2,921.84.
Gold closed at $326.15 in London, down from $327.85 on Wednesday. Silver ended a cent lower at $4.50.
